title: RTX 4090 engine keep-warm with a long spin: new sessions after 12-58 s idle prefill at back-to-back speed, outputs unchanged, about 72 W above idle while held
question: Built into ninfer-serve for sm_89 (alphastorm/ninfer 7fa2f80a: a single-warp spin of 50 ms every 100 ms instead of 3.5 ms every 10 ms), does --gpu-keep-warm-ms 60000 hold the RTX 4090 in P2 and bring new sessions after idle back to back-to-back speed with identical outputs?
prior_evidence: EXP-064 rejected the RTX 5090 pattern on this card (every session after a gap started in P8) and, in a sweep run after its rule decided, found that spins of 40 ms or more every 100 ms held P2 while spins of 3.5-6 ms every 10 ms did not. That sweep chose the pattern; it is not counted here.

decision_rule.arms: One sm_89 ninfer-serve built from alphastorm/ninfer 7fa2f80a, launched directly on the RTX 4090 host with the RTX 4090 lane's serving arguments exactly as in EXP-064: OFF without --gpu-keep-warm-ms, then ON with --gpu-keep-warm-ms 60000.
decision_rule.workload_per_arm: EXP-064's: one cold request that builds the stable prefix, then 30 new two-message sessions after gaps 0,12,0,25,0,38,0,53,0,58 s repeated three times; greedy, thinking off, 64 output tokens, identical prompts in both arms; nvidia-smi every 50 ms. Latency is the server's own prefill time from its request log.
decision_rule.regression: The OFF arm regresses if, at three or more of the five delays, its median prefill is at least 25% and at least 75 ms above its back-to-back median.
decision_rule.recovery: The ON arm recovers if, at every delay, its median prefill is within 10% and within 20 ms of its back-to-back median, and every session after a gap starts in P2.
decision_rule.safety: All 31 responses are byte-identical between the arms and to EXP-064's OFF arm, no request fails, and the ON arm's back-to-back median prefill is at most 10% above the OFF arm's.
decision_rule.decision: If regression, recovery and safety all hold, the RTX 4090 profile ships engine.gpu_keep_warm_ms = 60000 on a component built from this source; otherwise it ships 0.
decision_rule.informational: Power while held (ON arm gaps) against idle (OFF arm gaps); not a gate.

pre_registration.note: The rule was committed and pushed before either arm ran. After the run, the host name in the arms text was replaced by a neutral description because the product verifier forbids private host markers; the rule is otherwise unchanged.

answer: Yes. With the sm_89 spin of 50 ms every 100 ms, --gpu-keep-warm-ms 60000 held the RTX 4090 in P2 through every gap of up to 58 s (every one of 9,004 samples in the gaps was P2, at 50% GPU utilization and 77.5 W against about 5 W idle in P8), and every session after 12-58 s idle prefilled in 0.1461-0.1481 s (TTFT 0.167-0.178 s), the same as back to back (median 0.147 s). Without it, sessions after the same gaps started in P8 and prefilled in 0.26-0.43 s (medians 0.336-0.399 s). All 31 outputs were byte-identical between the arms and to EXP-064's OFF arm, which ran the v0.8.3 source.
decision: Rule outcome: regression holds at 5 of 5 delays, recovery holds at every delay with every post-gap session starting in P2, and safety holds. The RTX 4090 profile ships engine.gpu_keep_warm_ms = 60000 on a component built from alphastorm/ninfer 7fa2f80a or a packaging-only descendant (v0.6.9-qwen38-4090-beta.1 from 5ac17674).

method.host: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (VBIOS 95.02.3c.c0.f4, 450 W limit), Windows 11, driver 610.88, CUDA 13.3; the lane's managed release stopped for the window and left stopped afterwards
method.build: alphastorm/ninfer 7fa2f80a, Release, sm_89, MSVC 14.44 and nvcc 13.3; ninfer-serve 792f1cac. Its keep-warm device test passed on this card: one spin 50.0 ms, and a launch while a spin runs is skipped (two launches 50.0 ms).
method.arms: EXP-064's launcher and serving arguments unchanged: OFF 15:39:10-15:50:28Z, ON with --gpu-keep-warm-ms 60000 15:50:45-16:01:40Z.
method.sampling: nvidia-smi on the host every 50 ms.

power.note: P2 samples under 60% utilization in the ON arm against EXP-064's P8 idle; comparable to the RTX 5090's about 71 W (EXP-062). The energy cost over a 60 s grace scales with how often requests arrive after a gap; EXP-062's replay of RTX 5090 production traffic put a 60 s grace at about 2.3 W average there.

limits: One card, one driver, one Windows host.
Arms ran OFF then ON, not interleaved; the effect (every post-gap session back at back-to-back speed, in P2) is far outside order effects.
Synthetic short prompts on a 15K-token prefix; production agent turns are larger.
The worker paces each 100 ms period on a condition variable; the measured 50% utilization shows the period ran as intended on this host.
Back-to-back sessions arrived while a spin could still run; their median did not move (0.147 s against 0.1466 s), but a request arriving mid-spin can overlap one warp for up to 50 ms.
